outcome.technical: _locks.py: I added _dir_mutex(ld, primitives=None), a contextlib context manager. It takes an exclusive kernel lock on MUTEX_NAME ('.mutex') in the lock directory: fcntl.flock LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB, polled, on POSIX; msvcrt.locking LK_NBLCK on byte 0 on Windows, released with LK_UNLCK. It is bounded by MUTEX_SECONDS (10.0). A mutex held past that bound raises OSError EBUSY naming the mutex, and an interpreter with neither fcntl nor msvcrt raises OSError ENOLCK naming both. Callers turn either refusal into their error answer. Every claim-file mutation now runs under the mutex. _claim does its exists pre-check, then calls _place_claim (the old body) under the mutex. _take_over makes the stamp check, the unlink and the exclusive create in one hold, through _swap_claim. release reads through _read_stamped and removes through _remove_claim, which re-checks the stamp under the mutex and answers removed, gone or changed; changed is E_LIVE and nothing is removed. _write_lock now runs under the mutex. _claim_stamp now also carries the file's bytes. claim_path(ld, name) is new and public. No liveness probe runs under the mutex; the probes come first, and the stamp (bytes included) is re-checked under it. No rename/put-back sequence. drive-phase.py: _marked_any_start reads a mark's value whatever start it was taken under. launch_base and the measure-base drop use it, so release_replaced gives back an earlier start's launch claim. release_orphan_claims runs at the end of sweep_base_trees. It gives back each base- claim of the phase whose launch no mark names, once _locks.holder_gone reads its holder gone, and writes a did-line for each. _lock_alphabet is now shared by base_progress_path and the prefix. _doctor_hygiene.abandoned_advice now leads with 'it may be deleted once no base-run of it is live', and gives the reclaim clause only on the condition that the launch is still the current one. The docstring says why. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: a new paragraph states the mutex semantics, Windows included. The takeover paragraph now says the stamp carries bytes and that the check, removal and create are one hold. The doctor-advice passage and the base-claim passage (orphan sweep, earlier start, lc11-lc14) are corrected. Fixtures adjusted: tk5's sneak-in planted its claim with _write_lock, which would now wait on the mutex the takeover holds, so it writes the winner plainly. test_drive_phase's _bk_files leaves out the mutex file, which is the directory's own file and not something a dead run leaves. Sweep: 24/24 files ok, 6722 cases; then test__doctor_report and test__worktrees, 2/2 ok. SECURITY.md was read and NOT edited: its lock sentences (the fail-mode table, and 'a lock name is a coordination convention, not an access boundary') still hold as written. One fact the orchestrator may want stated there, in a file this task does not declare: any local process that can open .mutex can hold it, and every claim change in that clone then fails open with E_ERR after MUTEX_SECONDS. The Windows half: mx11 drives the msvcrt branch through a stand-in module on this machine. mx5-mx8 run unchanged on the Windows CI leg against the real msvcrt; that run has not been seen here. Dependants: _evidence_io, _invariants, _proc_group, audit-lock, stamp-verification, _proposals and audit-task import _locks. Their public API is unchanged except that release can now answer E_LIVE for a claim that changed while the release was decided, or 0 with a let-go line. Each one's suite is green in the sweep above. _age_minutes, _displaced_record and _identity are unchanged. _claim_stamp gained the bytes, and tk0/tk0b still pass. The drive-phase dependants (drive-without-model, _worktrees, test__filed_returns and the rest) get only added functions. test_drive_without_model, test_commit_task_work, test_audit_status and test__worktrees are green. The README, reference and orchestrator prose name decisions this change does not touch. _doctor_hygiene's dependants: audit-doctor.py calls check_locks, whose signature is unchanged, and test__doctor_report is green. The guide's passage was updated. test__locks dependants: test_run_test_gate (_cases/_selftest) is green; .github/sweep-costs.json was NOT re-recorded for the new mx block, which adds two-process races of about 2 s each. test_drive_phase dependants: the lc-block grew by four cases.
outcome.descriptive: Every change to a claim file now runs under one kernel-held mutex per lock directory, so two takers, or a release and a takeover, can no longer both act on one judged claim. Base-run claims of replaced launches, from earlier starts or killed later, are given back, and the doctor's advice no longer promises a reclaim that a replaced launch never makes.
